title: Mapping the Token Depth Boundary of Safety Alignment Across Model Families

original_idea.problem: The exact token depth at which alignment kicks in and how this varies across model families is uncharacterized.
original_idea.direction: Force models to output forced prefixes of increasing length, then measure at what prefix length harmful content generation drops. Plot ASR vs. prefix depth per model.
original_idea.why_it_matters: A cheap mapping experiment could guide defense prioritization across the open-source model ecosystem.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: token depth mapping -> identifies which models have shallow vs deep alignment -> guides defense prioritization. Clear, actionable safety output.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inference-only experiment using forced prefixes via Ollama or HuggingFace API. Standard tools, clear procedure. Guided-level: a beginner can execute with instructions.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: ASR vs prefix depth plot for each model family. Single precise experiment with well-defined success criteria. Can go from start to result quickly.

novelty.reasoning: This idea is substantially covered by existing work. Qi et al. (ICLR 2025) already mapped KL divergence decay across token positions for aligned vs. base models, establishing the shallow alignment phenomenon. The Prefill-Based Jailbreak paper (arXiv:2504.21038) tested prefilling attacks across 14 models, reporting ASR curves. The shallow-vs-deep-alignment repository (GitHub: Unispac) provides code for these experiments. 'Any-Depth Alignment' (arXiv:2510.18081) and the gradient analysis paper (arXiv:2603.04851) further characterize depth boundaries. While the specific ASR-vs-prefix-depth plot across open-source model families is a useful replication, the methodology and core findings are well-established.
